The service is instrumented for collection, not for judgement: it publishes metrics, exports traces and
logs, and defines no dashboard, no objective and no alert threshold.

### 5.1 Actuator endpoints

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:57 -->

The web exposure list contains 4 endpoints. Health and info are public;
env and prometheus fall through to the authenticated-request rule, so reading them needs a token.

| Endpoint | Exposed | Endpoint-level option |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | yes | — |
| `info` | yes | — |
| `env` | yes | enabled = `true` |
| `prometheus` | yes | — |

: Actuator endpoints on the web exposure list.



<!-- evidence: services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:56 -->

The configuration also declares `management.metrics.export.prometheus.enabled`. What answers
`/actuator/prometheus` in the scrape format is the Prometheus registry the build puts on the
classpath, together with that endpoint sitting on the exposure list; the declared key is the
meter-export switch under the name Spring Boot dropped before version 3, so the line states an intent
the framework no longer reads. GAP-3 records it.
<!-- evidence: services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:55, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:57 -->

### 5.2 The OpenTelemetry agent

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/build.gradle:220, services/shopping/build.gradle:222, services/shopping/build.gradle:226, services/shopping/build.gradle:237, services/shopping/build.gradle:238, services/shopping/build.gradle:239, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:36, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:38, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:40, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:42, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:44, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:46, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:48, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:50, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:52 -->

The image always carries `opentelemetry-javaagent.jar` version `2.17.0` and starts the JVM with
the agent attached, so no overlay can deploy the service without it. The collector address, the
protocol, the exporters and the sampler come from environment variables, and only the
`k3d` overlay declares them.

| Variable | Value | Declared by |
|---|---|---|
| `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` | `-javaagent:/app/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `shopping` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | `http://otel-collector:4317` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | `grpc` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` | `otlp` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` | `otlp` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` | `none` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` | `parentbased_traceidratio` | `k3d` overlay |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` | `1.0` | `k3d` overlay |

: Telemetry settings the deployment declares.
<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:36, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:38, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:40, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:42, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:44, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:46, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:48, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:50, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:52 -->

Traces and logs are exported over gRPC to the collector endpoint and sampled at a ratio of one; the
metrics exporter is set to `none`, which is why the prometheus endpoint above, and not the agent, is
where metrics leave the process.

### 5.3 The collector the repository ships

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:15, services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:31, services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:122, services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:86 -->

The collector is an object of this repository but not of the application overlay: one replica, its
pipeline read from a ConfigMap, receiving OTLP over gRPC and HTTP on the ports the agent points at.

| Exporter | File | Rotation |
|---|---|---|
| `debug` | the collector's own log | — |
| `file/traces` | `/var/lib/otel/traces.jsonl` | 50 MB, 7 days |
| `file/logs` | `/var/lib/otel/logs.jsonl` | 50 MB, 7 days |

: Exporters of the collector pipeline.


Each pipeline is a straight line from the OTLP receiver to one file: traces to the traces file, logs to
the logs file, and the debug exporter echoing both to the collector's log. Nothing samples on the
collector side and nothing forwards the files anywhere — they are written into a volume that exists
only as long as the collector pod does, so a restart of that pod discards the telemetry, and the
rotation above bounds the file size rather than the retention anybody can read. GAP-4 records it.
<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:122, services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:86 -->

### 5.4 Log levels

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:60, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:61, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:62, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:63, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:64, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:65, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:66, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:67, services/shopping/src/main/resources/application.yml:68 -->

The application configuration sets a level per logger for framework loggers only; no logger of the
service itself is listed, so the root level of the framework applies to it.

| Logger | Level |
|---|---|
| `org.apache.catalina.startup.DigesterFactory` | `ERROR` |
| `org.apache.catalina.util.LifecycleBase` | `ERROR` |
| `org.apache.coyote.http11.Http11NioProtocol` | `WARN` |
| `org.apache.sshd.common.util.SecurityUtils` | `WARN` |
| `org.apache.tomcat.util.net.NioSelectorPool` | `WARN` |
| `org.eclipse.jetty.util.component.AbstractLifeCycle` | `ERROR` |
| `org.hibernate.validator.internal.util.Version` | `WARN` |
| `org.springframework.boot.actuate.endpoint.jmx` | `WARN` |
| `org.springframework.web` | `INFO` |

: Log levels declared by the application configuration.



The image sets `SPRING_OUTPUT_ANSI_ENABLED` to `never`, so the container log is plain text, and the
image environment is also where the agent is attached. Both settings arrive with the image, so no
manifest has to repeat them.
<!-- evidence: services/shopping/build.gradle:241, services/shopping/build.gradle:242 -->

### 5.5 What the repository does not define

- **No dashboard.** No dashboard definition of any kind is checked in, so nothing prepares a view of this
  telemetry. GAP-1 records it.
- **No alert threshold.** No alerting rule and no threshold is declared anywhere in the repository, so
  nothing in the repository says when a human should be woken. GAP-2 records it.
- **No service-level objective.** No objective and no error-budget target is stated, so there is no
  agreed measure of whether the service is doing its job. GAP-5 records it.
- **No durable telemetry store.** The collector writes to a volume scoped to its own pod and forwards
  nothing, so traces and logs survive a collector restart only if something outside this repository
  reads the files first (GAP-4).
